gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ the flames with buckets for an hour by the time the firemen arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour by the time … arrived' — past perfect continuous for duration before a past moment.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the dentist on Thursday afternoon — I booked it last week.
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am seeing.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the same bus to work every morning, even in winter.
gaps.hint: every morning signals a fixed routine
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' describes a fixed routine, which takes the present simple: catches.

gaps.sentence: This is the second time the printer ___ down this week.
gaps.explanation: 'This is the second time …' is followed by the present perfect.

gaps.sentence: It ___ hard when we left the house, so we took our umbrellas.
gaps.hint: background weather at the moment we left
gaps.explanation: The rain was in progress as a background situation when we left, so the past continuous fits: was raining.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.
